disease.label: CLN6 disease
disease.summary: A rare inherited brain disease of childhood with seizures, vision loss and loss of movement and speech skills.

phenotypes.label: Developmental regression
phenotypes.summary: Losing skills (speech, walking, learning) that a child had already gained.

phenotypes.label: Seizure
phenotypes.summary: Sudden bursts of abnormal electrical activity in the brain (fits).

mechanisms.label: Lysosomal degradation (ceroid lipofuscin storage)
mechanisms.summary: Cells break down worn-out parts inside lysosomes. In all NCLs this recycling fails and waste (lipofuscin) builds up, especially in nerve cells.

disease.label: CLN2 disease
disease.summary: A form of Batten disease that starts in toddlers with seizures and loss of skills. An enzyme replacement therapy is approved.

caution: CLN2 disease has an approved enzyme replacement therapy (cerliponase alfa) because TPP1 is a soluble lysosomal enzyme that can be supplied from outside the cell. That success does not automatically transfer to CLN5 disease: whether CLN5 can be replaced the same way is unproven.

disease.label: CLN3 disease
disease.summary: The most common form of Batten disease. It usually starts at school age with vision loss, followed by seizures and loss of skills.

caution: CLN3 is a lysosomal membrane protein, not a soluble enzyme. Similar symptoms do not mean similar treatments: enzyme-replacement-style approaches are not expected to work for CLN3.

disease.label: MOCK ultra-rare NCL subtype X (fictional)
disease.summary: A FICTIONAL, made-up ultra-rare Batten-like disease used to demo the 'no known group' case. Not a real diagnosis.

caution: Subtype X is only known from a few families; similarity is based on two symptoms and an inferred mechanism.
